external_entities.name: Execution Layer Engine
external_entities.description: Execution client that validates payload correctness including block access list interpretation

ambiguities.text: The specification defines block_access_list as ByteList[MAX_BYTES_PER_TRANSACTION] but does not specify the exact RLP encoding format or schema of the access list contents.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the access list follows the same format as EIP-2930 transaction access lists (list of [address, storage_keys] tuples) encoded in RLP. This needs verification against the EIP-7928 EIP text.

ambiguities.text: It is unclear whether the execution engine validates the block_access_list contents or just the execution payload as a whole.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the execution engine validates the entire payload including access list correctness as part of verify_and_notify_new_payload. The consensus layer only commits the merkle root.

implicit_assumptions.description: The execution engine is trusted to correctly validate block access list data and return accurate VALID/INVALID responses.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A compromised or buggy execution engine could accept invalid access lists, leading to incorrect state roots and potential consensus failures.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Engine API connection between consensus and execution layers is secure and authenticated.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A MITM attack on the Engine API could forge VALID responses for invalid payloads, causing the consensus layer to accept malicious blocks.
